TECHNOVA 
Grievance_and_Escalation_Procedure 2026 
Effective Date: June 15, 2026 
Version: 2.0 
Approved By: Chief Human Resources Officer (CHRO). 

1.0 Our Commitment to a Fair Workplace 
1.1 Purpose and Philosophy 
At Technova, we are dedicated to fostering a positive, respectful, and productive work environment 
where every employee feels valued and heard. This Grievance and Escalation Procedure is designed 
to provide a clear, fair, and consistent framework for raising and resolving workplace concerns. 
Our philosophy is that open communication and early resolution are the most effective ways to 
address issues. We believe that by providing a structured and transparent process, we can address 
conflicts constructively, reinforce our company values, and ensure that all employees are treated 
with dignity and respect. This procedure serves as a core tool to help us uphold our commitment to a 
healthy workplace culture. 
1.2 Scope of This Policy 
This policy applies to all regular full-time and part-time employees of Technova. It covers any 
concern, problem, or complaint that an employee may have regarding their work, the work 
environment, or their employment relationship. This includes, but is not limited to, issues related to 
working conditions, treatment by managers or colleagues, and the application of company policies. 
1.3 Core Principles 
This procedure is founded on four essential principles that guide our approach at every stage: 
• 
Confidentiality: All grievances will be handled with the utmost discretion. Information will 
only be shared with those who have a legitimate need to know in order to investigate and 
resolve the concern. 
• 
Non-Retaliation: Technova has a strict zero-tolerance policy for retaliation. No employee will 
face adverse action, harassment, or discrimination for raising a grievance in good faith or for 
participating in an investigation. Any act of retaliation is a serious violation of company policy 
and will result in disciplinary action, up to and including termination. 
• 
Impartiality and Fairness: Every grievance will be investigated and reviewed objectively and 
impartially. Decisions will be based on a thorough and fair assessment of the facts. All parties 
involved will have an opportunity to present their side of the story. 
• 
Timeliness: We are committed to addressing all concerns promptly. This policy outlines 
specific timelines for each stage of the process to ensure that grievances are resolved 
without unnecessary delay. 
1.4 What is a Grievance?

A grievance is a formal complaint raised by an employee concerning a work-related issue that they 
believe is unfair, unjust, or in violation of company policy or legal standards. Examples of issues that 
may form the basis of a grievance include: 
• 
Perceived unfair or inequitable treatment. 
• 
Bullying, harassment, or discrimination. 
• 
Concerns about health and safety in the workplace. 
• 
Disputes over the interpretation or application of HR policies like leave and work hours. 
• 
Violations of the company's Code of Conduct. 
1.5 What is Not Covered by This Procedure? 
This procedure is not intended to address every type of workplace disagreement. The following 
issues are typically handled through separate, specific processes: 
• 
Disciplinary Action: Appeals against formal disciplinary warnings or actions. 
• 
Termination of Employment: Decisions related to the formal termination of employment. 
• 
Compensation Decisions: Issues related to salary, bonus amounts, or equity awards, which 
are managed through the annual compensation review process. 
• 
Performance Feedback: Disagreements with performance ratings or feedback received 
during a performance review. 
• 
Whistleblowing: Reports of illegal activity, financial malpractice, or serious dangers to public 
health, which should be raised under the company's Whistleblower Policy. 
2.0 Roles and Responsibilities 
A successful grievance process relies on the active and responsible participation of all parties 
involved. 
2.1 The Employee 
• 
To attempt, where appropriate, to resolve concerns informally at the earliest opportunity. 
• 
To raise formal grievances in a timely and factual manner, providing all relevant information. 
• 
To cooperate fully with any investigation. 
• 
To maintain strict confidentiality throughout the entire process. 
2.2 The Manager 
• 
To foster an environment where employees feel comfortable raising concerns. 
• 
To listen actively and take all coworker concerns seriously. 
• 
To make genuine efforts to resolve issues informally and promptly. 
• 
To participate constructively in formal investigations when required. 
• 
To uphold the core principles of confidentiality and non-retaliation.

2.3 The Human Resources (HR) Department 
• 
To act as an impartial steward of the grievance procedure. 
• 
To provide advice and support to both employees and managers throughout the process. 
• 
To ensure all formal grievances are properly documented, investigated, and resolved in 
accordance with this policy. 
• 
To appoint trained and completely impartial investigators. 
• 
To maintain secure records of all grievance proceedings. 
2.4 The Grievance Committee 
A formal Grievance Committee may be convened to hear appeals. The Committee typically consists 
of a senior HR leader, a senior leader from a neutral department, and another impartial manager. 
The Committee's role is to provide a final, objective review of the grievance and the initial decision. 
3.0 Informal Grievance Resolution 
3.1 The Value of Informal Resolution 
We strongly encourage employees to try and resolve concerns informally before initiating a formal 
grievance. Many workplace issues arise from simple misunderstandings or miscommunications and 
can often be resolved quickly and effectively through direct conversation. An informal approach can 
help preserve working relationships and find mutually agreeable solutions without the need for a 
lengthy formal process. 
3.2 Step-by-Step Informal Process 
• 
Reflect and Prepare: Before approaching anyone, take a moment to clearly identify the 
issue. What specifically is the problem, and what is your desired outcome? 
• 
Speak with Your Manager: Your direct manager is usually the best first point of contact. 
Schedule a private meeting to discuss your concerns openly and professionally. 
• 
Alternative Contact: If you are not comfortable speaking with your manager, or if your 
concern is about your manager, you can approach their manager or an HR Business Partner 
for an informal discussion. 
• 
Discussion and Agreement: The goal of the informal discussion is to reach a shared 
understanding and agree on a path forward, which could involve clarifying expectations, 
changing a process, or simply having a constructive dialogue. 
3.3 The Role of Mediation 
In some cases, a facilitated conversation with a neutral third party can be helpful. HR can act as an 
impartial mediator to help employees and managers discuss their issues and find common ground. 
Mediation is a voluntary process aimed at achieving a mutually acceptable resolution. 
3.4 Informal Resolution Case Study: Recognizing Contributions 
• 
Scenario: Alex, a graphic designer, feels that his colleague, Ben, is consistently taking credit 
for his ideas in team meetings, which is causing friction and demotivating Alex.

• 
Action: Instead of immediately filing a complaint, Alex schedules a one-on-one meeting with 
his manager, Sarah. He calmly explains the situation with specific examples and states that 
his desired outcome is fair recognition. Sarah listens, validates his feelings, and agrees to 
observe team dynamics. She also has a separate coaching conversation with Ben about 
teamwork and acknowledging contributors. 
• 
Outcome: In subsequent meetings, Sarah asks for input from all team members, and Ben 
becomes more mindful of giving credit. Alex feels heard and respected, and the issue is 
resolved without damaging the working relationship. 
4.0 Formal Grievance Procedure 
4.1 When to Initiate a Formal Grievance 
A formal grievance should be initiated when an attempt at informal resolution has been 
unsuccessful, the nature of the grievance is too serious for an informal approach, or the grievance is 
against your direct manager and you are not comfortable addressing it with them informally. 
4.2 Step-by-Step Formal Process 
• 
Step 1: Filing a Formal Grievance: To begin the formal process, the employee must submit a 
written grievance to the HR department using the official Grievance Form. The submission 
should include a detailed description of the event, relevant dates, locations, witnesses, 
supporting evidence, and your desired outcome. 
• 
Step 2: Acknowledgment and Assessment: HR will acknowledge receipt of the formal 
grievance in writing within two (2) working days. HR will then conduct an initial assessment 
and appoint an impartial investigator. 
• 
Step 3: Formal Investigation: The investigator will conduct a thorough and objective 
investigation, interviewing the grievant, the respondent, and relevant witnesses, while 
reviewing documents like emails and company records privately. 
• 
Step 4: Grievance Meeting: After the investigation is complete, a formal grievance meeting 
will be scheduled and chaired by an uninvolved manager. The employee has the right to be 
accompanied at this meeting by a work colleague or a certified trade union representative. 
• 
Step 5: Decision and Notification: Following the meeting, the chairperson will consider all 
the evidence and communicate the final decision and corrective remedies in writing, 
typically within five (5) working days. 
4.3 Target Timelines for the Formal Process 
• 
Acknowledgment of Grievance: 2 working days. 
• 
Completion of Investigation: 15 working days. 
• 
Grievance Meeting: Within 5 working days of investigation completion. 
• 
Written Decision: Within 5 working days of the meeting. 
4.4 Formal Process Case Study: Promotion Discrepancies

• 
Scenario: Maria, an employee in the finance department, believes she was overlooked for a 
promotion in favor of a less-qualified colleague, feeling it is a case of bias. She loses trust in 
her manager and files a formal grievance. 
• 
Action: Maria completes the Grievance Form, citing specific projects and performance 
metrics. HR acknowledges it within two days and assigns a senior HR specialist to investigate. 
The investigator interviews Maria, her manager, and the promoted colleague, and reviews 
interview notes and promotion criteria. A meeting is held, chaired by the Director of Finance, 
which Maria attends with a colleague for support. 
• 
Outcome: The investigation concludes that the selection process lacked clear, objective 
scoring, leading to the appearance of bias. The Director upholds part of the grievance, 
committing to a detailed development plan for Maria and a mandate for the department to 
implement a more structured promotion process. 
5.0 Escalation and Appeal Process 
5.1 The Right to Appeal 
If an employee is not satisfied with the outcome of the formal grievance procedure, they have the 
right to appeal the decision. An appeal is not a re-investigation of the grievance but a review of the 
original decision and the process used to reach it. 
5.2 Grounds for an Appeal 
An appeal may be submitted on one or more of the following grounds: 
• 
New evidence has come to light that was not available during the original investigation. 
• 
There was a significant flaw in the procedure followed, which may have affected the 
outcome. 
• 
The decision or the resulting action was not reasonable or proportionate based on the 
findings. 
5.3 How to Submit an Appeal 
An employee wishing to appeal must do so in writing to the HR department within five (5) working 
days of receiving the formal grievance decision. The written appeal must clearly state the specific 
grounds on which the appeal is being made. 
5.4 The Appeal Hearing and Final Decision 
The appeal will be heard by an Appeal Panel consisting of a senior leader not previously involved and 
the Grievance Committee. The employee will be invited to present their case and retains the right to 
be accompanied by a colleague or union representative. 
The decision of the Appeal Panel is final, and there is no further internal right of appeal. The final 
decision will be communicated to the employee in writing within five (5) working days of the appeal 
hearing. 
5.5 Appeal Process Case Study: Strengthening Remedies 
• 
Scenario: In the case above, Maria is not satisfied with the remedy offered, feeling a 
development plan alone does not address the core issue of bias in the promotion decision.

• 
Action: Maria submits a written appeal within five days. An Appeal Panel is convened, 
chaired by the company's Chief Human Resources Officer (CHRO). At the appeal hearing, 
Maria argues her case. 
• 
Outcome: The Appeal Panel reviews the case and agrees that the remedy should be 
strengthened. The panel's final decision includes a formal written apology and mandates that 
Maria be automatically included in the interview pool for the next relevant promotion 
opportunity. This decision is final. 
6.0 Handling Specific Types of Grievances 
6.1 Grievances Involving a Direct Manager 
If a grievance is about an employee's direct manager, the employee is not required to address it with 
them informally. The formal grievance should be submitted directly to the next level of management 
or to an HR Business Partner. 
6.2 Harassment, Bullying, or Discrimination 
Allegations of harassment, bullying, or discrimination are taken extremely seriously. These grievances 
will always be handled through the formal procedure and will be investigated by specially trained HR 
professionals or external investigators. These investigations are governed by the company's separate 
Anti-Harassment and Equal Employment Opportunity policies. 
6.3 Collective Grievances vs. Whistleblowing 
• 
Collective Grievances: If a group of employees shares the same grievance, they may submit 
it collectively. One or two employees should be nominated as spokespersons for the group to 
liaise with HR throughout the process. 
• 
Whistleblowing Distinction: A grievance typically relates to an employee's personal 
circumstances or treatment. A whistleblowing complaint involves reporting information that 
is in the public interest, such as criminal activity, corruption, or serious dangers, which 
should be raised under the company's separate Whistleblower Policy. 
7.0 Confidentiality and Data Protection 
7.1 Maintaining Confidentiality 
All individuals involved in a grievance procedure—the grievant, the respondent, witnesses, 
managers, and HR—are required to maintain strict confidentiality. Breaches of confidentiality can 
undermine the integrity of the process and may result in disciplinary action. 
7.2 Data Protection and Record-Keeping 
HR will create and maintain a confidential case file for each formal grievance. This file will be stored 
securely and separately from the employee's main personnel file. Access will be restricted strictly to 
authorized HR and legal personnel, and all records will be managed in compliance with data 
protection laws. 
8.0 Policy Review and Training 
8.1 Policy Review Framework

This policy will be reviewed by the HR department every two years, or more frequently if required by 
changes in legislation, to ensure it remains effective and fully compliant. 
8.2 Training and Awareness 
All managers will receive mandatory training on this policy and on their role in handling workplace 
concerns effectively and empathetically. The policy will be made available to all employees via the 
company's intranet, and it will be covered thoroughly during new hire orientation. 
9.0 Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs) 
Q1: Do I have to talk to my manager before filing a formal grievance? A: While we strongly 
encourage informal resolution first, you are not required to speak with your manager if you are 
uncomfortable doing so or if your grievance is about them. In that case, you can go directly to HR. 
Q2: Will filing a grievance negatively impact my career? A: Absolutely not. Our non-retaliation 
policy is strictly enforced. It is a serious violation of company policy to penalize an employee in any 
way for raising a concern in good faith. 
Q3: Can I remain anonymous when I file a grievance? A: Due to the need to conduct a thorough 
investigation, it is generally not possible to remain completely anonymous when filing a formal 
grievance. However, we will maintain confidentiality to the greatest extent possible. 
Q4: How long does the formal grievance process take? A: We aim to complete the entire formal 
process, from filing to decision, within approximately 25-30 working days. However, complex cases 
may take longer. 
Q5: Who can I bring with me to a grievance or appeal meeting? A: You have the right to be 
accompanied by a single individual who is a current work colleague or a certified trade union 
representative. They are there for support and are not permitted to answer questions on your behalf. 
Q6: What happens if my grievance is not upheld? A: If your grievance is not upheld, HR will still offer 
support and may suggest mediation or other actions to help repair working relationships and move 
forward constructively. 
Q7: Can I withdraw my grievance after I have filed it? A: Yes, you can withdraw your grievance at 
any stage by notifying HR in writing. However, in cases involving serious allegations, the company 
may be obligated to continue the investigation regardless. 
10.0 Formal Grievance Form Framework 
The official, downloadable Formal Grievance Form is securely hosted on our internal HR portal. For 
reference, the structured data input fields required for filing include: 
• 
Employee Details: Full Name, Employee ID, Department, Direct Manager's Name, and Date 
of Submission. 
• 
Section 1: Details of the Grievance: A detailed description of the grievance including specific 
facts, dates, times, locations, individuals involved, and names of any witnesses. 
• 
Section 2: Informal Resolution Attempts: A descriptive summary of any steps already taken 
to resolve the matter informally. 
• 
Section 3: Desired Resolution: A clear description of the specific outcome you are seeking to 
resolve the workplace concern.

• 
Section 4: Supporting Documentation: A list of all physical or digital documents (e.g., emails, 
files, messages) provided to support the filing. 
• 
Sign-off Block: Employee physical or electronic signature and date lines.

Welcome to the team! At Technova, we build simple, clear, and impactful technology solutions.

our growing organization.

1.2 Purpose of This Handbook 
This Employee Handbook provides you with essential everyday information about Technova. It 
acts as a central reference point for our company procedures, core benefits, and behavioral 
standards. While this guide is broad, it cannot anticipate every unique situation. The policies 
outlined here may change over time to adapt to new business goals and legal standards. You 
can always find the absolute latest version of this document on our internal HR portal. 
1.3 Our Commitment to You 
Technova is dedicated to building a supportive work experience centered around four 
foundational ideas: 
• 
Fairness: We treat every single employee with equal consistency, dignity, and respect. 
• 
Opportunity: We actively provide clear pathways for your long-term professional growth. 
• 
Inclusion: We value unique voices and ensure everyone feels safe contributing their ideas. 
• 
Well-being: We actively look out for your health, safety, and personal work-life balance. 
1.4 Employment-at-Will 
Employment at Technova is strictly on an at-will basis where permitted by law. This means that 
either you or Technova can choose to end the employment relationship at any time, for any 
reason, with or without prior notice. This handbook does not serve as an official employment 
contract and does not guarantee employment for any specific length of time.

2.0 Our Company, Our Culture 
Our workplace culture defines how we interact, solve problems, and grow together. We focus on 
transparency over bureaucracy and action over complex processes. 
2.1 Our Mission, Vision, and Values 
Our Mission is to simplify complex challenges using intelligent, modern technology solutions. 
Our Vision is to be a trusted global partner in engineering excellence, recognized for our 
commitment to quality and integrity. 
Our Core Values include: 
• 
Customer Obsession: We listen intently to our clients and design our solutions around their 
real needs. 
• 
Absolute Integrity: We focus on doing the right thing in every situation, keeping 
communications honest and clear. 
• 
Continuous Innovation: We actively seek simpler, smarter ways to solve everyday problems. 
• 
One Team Collaboration: We support one another across departments, celebrating our wins 
together. 
• 
Operational Excellence: We hold our work to high professional standards and always strive 
for exceptional outcomes. 
2.2 Our History 
Technova was founded with a foundational goal: to make advanced technology highly 
accessible and straightforward for businesses everywhere. What started as a dedicated small 
team has quickly evolved into a fast-growing enterprise serving a diverse, global client base. 
Our ongoing journey is fueled entirely by technical passion, iterative learning, and a shared 
commitment to sustainable growth. 
2.3 Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion (DEI) 
We know that a diverse team brings better ideas and a stronger workspace. DEI is a core part 
of who we are. We intentionally create an environment where every employee has a fair 
opportunity to thrive, regardless of their background. This mindset applies directly to our hiring, 
promotion, daily compensation, and training practices.

3.0 Your Employment 
This section covers the standard guidelines, classifications, and basic administrative 
components regarding your employment at Technova. 
3.1 Equal Employment Opportunity 
Technova is a dedicated Equal Opportunity Employer. We extend equal employment 
opportunities to all team members and applicants without regard to race, color, religion, sex, 
national origin, age, physical or mental disability, veteran status, or any other characteristic 
protected by applicable local laws. 
3.2 Employee Classifications 
For benefits eligibility and clear payroll administration, we classify our roles as follows: 
• 
Full-Time: Team members scheduled to work our standard 40-hour workweek. They qualify 
for all company-sponsored benefits. 
• 
Part-Time: Team members scheduled to work fewer than 30 hours per week. Benefit 
eligibility for these roles is determined by individual employment agreements. 
• 
Exempt: Employees working in professional or managerial roles who are exempt from 
standard overtime pay provisions and receive a fixed salary. 
• 
Non-Exempt: Employees who are eligible for overtime pay for any hours physically worked 
beyond 40 within a standard workweek. 
3.3 Probationary Period 
Your first 90 days of employment serve as an introductory probationary period. This window 
gives both you and your manager a fair opportunity to see if the role is a great match for your 
skills and our culture. Regular feedback will be provided during this time. 
3.4 Your Employee File 
The HR Department securely maintains a personnel file for every employee. This file contains 
key documents like your original application, role updates, performance reviews, and salary 
history. You can review your file at any time by coordinating an appointment with HR.

Technova Employee Handbook | Page 5 
3.5 Promotions and Transfers 
We love helping our team members grow. We actively encourage internal promotions and 
lateral transfers for open roles. Available positions are regularly published on our internal 
company job board. To apply for an internal transfer, you generally need to be in your current 
role for at least 12 months while maintaining a strong performance record. 
3.6 Performance Management 
Our performance review system is continuous and collaborative. It focuses on growth rather 
than rigid grading: 
• 
Goal Alignment: We set transparent annual goals that align with team objectives. 
• 
Regular Check-ins: Managers and employees have informal, ongoing discussions 
throughout the year. 
• 
Annual Review: A formal yearly conversation to evaluate key achievements, discuss 
feedback, and plan for your future career development. 
3.7 Separation of Employment 
When an employment relationship ends, we aim to make the transition clear and professional. 
• 
Voluntary Resignation: If you choose to leave Technova, we kindly ask that you submit a 
minimum of two weeks' written notice to your direct manager so we can transition your 
duties smoothly. 
• 
Involuntary Termination: In rare cases, the company may terminate employment due to 
prolonged poor performance, severe behavioral misconduct, or broader business 
restructuring.

4.0 Code of Conduct and Ethics 
We maintain a respectful, honest, and ethical workspace. This code outlines how we expect our 
team to represent themselves and Technova every day. 
4.1 Professional Conduct 
We expect every employee to act professionally and treat colleagues, clients, and partners with 
courtesy. Any disruptive, dishonest, or illegal behavior will not be tolerated and can result in 
disciplinary action up to termination. 
4.2 Anti-Harassment and Anti-Bullying 
Technova is committed to providing a workspace entirely free from harassment, discrimination, 
and bullying. We strictly prohibit unwelcome conduct or unfair treatment based on any legally 
protected personal traits. Bullying behavior that compromises an employee's well-being or 
safety has no place here. 
If you witness or experience harassment, report it immediately to HR or your manager. We 
investigate all reports promptly and confidentially. Technova strictly prohibits retaliation against 
anyone making a good-faith report. 
4.3 Conflicts of Interest 
A conflict of interest happens when your personal activities or relationships interfere with your 
ability to make objective decisions for Technova. You must avoid these situations. Common 
examples include: 
• 
Holding a significant financial stake in a direct competitor or vendor. 
• 
Using company resources or your professional title for personal financial gain. 
• 
Directly supervising or hiring a close family member without explicit HR approval. 
Please disclose any potential conflicts to HR as soon as you become aware of them.

Technova Employee Handbook | Page 7 
4.4 Gifts and Entertainment 
Exchanging modest business courtesies can build good relationships, but they must never 
influence objective business choices. 
• 
Receiving Gifts: You may accept minor, token items of nominal value. You must never 
accept cash, gift cards, or expensive personal items. 
• 
Business Entertainment: Standard meals and basic entertainment are acceptable if they 
have a direct, clear business purpose. 
4.5 Confidentiality and Intellectual Property 
While working at Technova, you will handle proprietary information, including code bases, 
customer data, and strategic roadmaps. You must keep this information completely secure and 
never share it outside the company. This duty continues even after your employment with us 
ends. All software, designs, ideas, and documentation you create as part of your job belong 
exclusively to Technova. 
4.6 Whistleblower Policy 
We strictly follow all relevant laws and ethics. If you see illegal practices or severe policy 
violations, report them immediately to HR or Legal. We will protect you completely; we do not 
tolerate any form of retaliation against employees who speak up in good faith. 
4.7 Ethics Case Study: Managing Conflicts 
Scenario: A procurement lead needs to pick a vendor for office equipment. Their sibling 
runs a local supply business that submits a competitive bid. 

Analysis: Even if the sibling's bid offers excellent value, the family connection creates a 
clear appearance of a conflict of interest. 

Correct Action: The procurement lead must immediately notify their manager and HR in 
writing. They must remove themselves entirely from the evaluation and voting process so 
the company can make an unbiased decision.

5.0 Workplace Policies 
Our daily operational guidelines ensure an organized, safe, and productive environment for all 
teams. 
5.1 Working Hours, Breaks, and Overtime 
• 
Standard Hours: Our core business operating hours are 9:00 AM to 5:30 PM, Monday 
through Friday, though hours may adjust slightly based on specific project needs. 
• 
Rest Breaks: Non-exempt team members receive a paid 15-minute break for every four 
hours worked, alongside a standard 30-minute unpaid meal break for shifts over five hours. 
Coordinate break times with your team to maintain smooth operations. 
• 
Overtime: Non-exempt employees receive overtime pay at 1.5 times their standard hourly 
rate for hours worked beyond 40 in a week. All overtime must be pre-approved by a 
manager. 
5.2 Attendance and Punctuality 
Reliable attendance keeps our projects running smoothly. If you expect to be late or absent, 
inform your manager directly before your scheduled start time. Unexcused, repetitive absences 
can lead to disciplinary action. 
5.3 Dress Code 
Our standard daily dress code is business casual. We trust your professional judgment to dress 
appropriately for a modern office. 
• 
Appropriate Clothing: Tailored trousers, khakis, neat jeans, casual button-downs, polo shirts, 
and blouses. 
• 
Items to Avoid: Ripped clothing, sportswear, beach footwear, or clothing featuring offensive 
language or graphics. 
• 
Client Engagements: Wear formal business attire when meeting face-to-face with clients or 
representing Technova at industry events.

5.4 Health and Safety 
Your physical well-being is our priority. Report all hazards, faulty equipment, or injuries to HR 
immediately. Take time to understand the emergency exit layouts and evacuation plans for your 
specific building. 
5.5 Drug and Alcohol-Free Workplace 
To keep our team safe and productive, we strictly prohibit the use, possession, or distribution of 
illegal drugs and alcohol on company property during work hours. Responsible consumption is 
permitted only at approved company-hosted evening social events where alcohol is formally 
served. 
5.6 Use of Company Technology and Assets 
Laptops, communication channels, and internet access provided by Technova are business 
tools. 
• 
Personal Use: Brief, occasional personal use is fine as long as it never impacts your work 
output or violates company security. 
• 
Privacy Expectations: Technova maintains the right to review and monitor company-owned 
networks and hardware. Employees should have no expectation of privacy regarding data 
created or stored on company systems. 
• 
Security Rules: Keep your devices secure, do not share passwords, and strictly follow our 
standard IT security protocols. 
5.7 Social Media Policy 
We respect your personal freedom to post online, but your words can impact Technova's 
reputation. 
• 
Protect Data: Never share private company details, source code, or internal plans online. 
• 
Be Respectful: Avoid posting content that discriminates against or defames Technova, your 
coworkers, or our clients. 
• 
Use Disclaimer: When discussing tech industry trends publicly, clearly state: 'The views 
expressed are my own and do not represent my employer.' 
5.8 Social Media Case Study: Online Activity 
Scenario: An employee posts a message on a public forum complaining about an 
unreleased system update, naming the project directly. 

Analysis: This violates our policy by disclosing internal project details and presenting

Correct Action: Project frustrations must be raised internally through managers or HR

6.0 Compensation and Benefits 
We provide competitive compensation packages that match industry benchmarks and reflect 
your professional skills, experience, and performance. 
6.1 Payroll Details 
Employees are paid on a consistent, predictable schedule. Direct deposit is mandatory for all 
team members, and detailed digital pay stubs are accessible at any time through our secure 
HRIS portal. 
6.2 Benefits Overview 
Technova provides a robust benefits plan to eligible full-time staff, which includes 
comprehensive medical insurance, retirement savings matches, life insurance options, and 
wellness program support. Full enrollment details can be accessed via the benefits portal. 
6.3 Travel Reimbursements 
The company reimburses all reasonable, pre-approved costs incurred during business travel. 
Ensure you submit detailed expense reports along with valid receipts within the required 
timeframe after your trip. 
7.0 Leave and Time Off 
We believe taking time off is vital for long-term productivity and personal health. 
• 
Paid Time Off (PTO): Full-time employees receive an annual allotment of PTO for vacations 
and personal time, scaling upwards with your tenure. 
• 
Sick Leave: We provide dedicated annual paid sick days to take care of your own health or 
look after an ill family member. 
• 
Holidays: Technova observes standard paid public holidays each calendar year, with the 
official schedule published every January. 
• 
Special Leave: We provide structured guidelines for parental leave, bereavement leave, and 
civic duties like jury duty.

8.0 Employee Development 
Continuous learning is central to our engineering mindset. We actively invest in your 
professional growth. 
8.1 Training and Development 
We support your career progression through multiple channels: 
• 
Giving you full access to digital learning and technical training platforms. 
• 
Organizing internal technical workshops and knowledge-sharing sessions. 
• 
Sponsoring attendance at key industry conferences and certification programs. 
8.2 Tuition Assistance 
Eligible employees can apply for financial assistance to complete degrees or professional 
certifications that directly align with their career path at Technova. Check the HR portal to view 
application rules and reimbursement caps. 
9.0 Problem Resolution and Communication 
We believe in open dialogue and fixing workplace problems quickly and transparently. 
9.1 Open Door Policy 
We maintain an active Open Door Policy. We encourage you to discuss your ideas, career 
goals, or workplace problems directly with your manager. If you feel uncomfortable doing so, 
you are always welcome to bring your thoughts to higher management or the HR team. 
9.2 Grievance Procedure 
When informal talks do not resolve an issue, you can file a formal complaint through our HR 
department. This ensures a structured, neutral, and fair investigation to find a clear solution. 
10.0 Acknowledgment of Receipt 
Every employee must sign an acknowledgment form on their first day or after major policy 
changes. This confirms you have received the handbook, understand where to find company 
policies, and agree to follow these workplace guidelines during your time with Technova.

TECHNOVA 
Leave Policy 2026 

Effective Date: January 1, 2026 
Version: 1.0 
Approved By: Board of Directors

Introduction and Scope 
1.0 Introduction 
At Technova, we believe that clear guidelines regarding time off help maintain both professional 
clarity and personal well-being. 
1.1 Purpose and Scope 
This document defines the official leave policies and procedural frameworks for all employees at 
Technova. The clear goal of this policy is to deliver a fair, transparent, and consistent system for 
managing employee time off. It ensures that every team member understands their personal time 
entitlements and the exact steps required to submit a request. This framework supports personal 
well-being while protecting day-to-day business operations and client deadlines. This policy 
completely supersedes any previous leave agreements, whether written or spoken. 
1.2 Our Philosophy on Work-Life Balance 
We recognize that our people are Technova’s most valuable asset. We are fully committed to 
fostering an open, supportive work environment that highlights a healthy work-life balance. 
Adequate rest and regular time away from work are essential for long-term health, daily morale, 
creative engagement, and engineering productivity. Our leave guidelines provide the flexibility 
needed to handle family needs, explore personal interests, and return to work recharged. 
1.3 Applicability 
This policy applies directly to all full-time and part-time permanent employees of Technova. 
Contractual staff, temporary workers, and interns may operate under different leave terms outlined 
specifically in their individual employment agreements. Provisions may adjust dynamically based on 
local labor laws in the jurisdictions where we operate. In any scenario where a conflict arises, local 
labor law will take priority. 
1.4 Key Definitions 
• 
Employee: Any individual employed by Technova on a permanent full-time or part-time 
basis. 
• 
Manager: A team member holding direct supervisory responsibility for other employees. 
• 
HR Department: The internal Human Resources department at Technova. 
• 
HRIS: The Human Resources Information System platform used to log requests and manage 
leave balances. 
• 
Leave Year: The official twelve-month calculation cycle, running from January 1st to 
December 31st. 
• 
Accrual: The ongoing process of earning time-off credits over a set period of service. 
• 
Medical Practitioner: A licensed and registered doctor or healthcare professional.

General Leave Guidelines 
2.0 General Leave Provisions 
These standard provisions govern how leave is tracked, submitted, and managed throughout the 
calendar year. 
2.1 The Leave Year 
The official leave year at Technova matches the calendar year, beginning January 1, 2026, and 
concluding December 31, 2026. All calculations are based on this window. For any employee joining 
Technova mid-year, their time-off entitlements will be prorated based on their remaining months of 
active service. 
2.2 Procedure for Requesting Leave 
All time-off requests, excluding sudden emergencies like illness, must be submitted in advance 
through the company's HRIS portal. When logging a request, employees must clearly input the 
specific leave type, start date, end date, and any helpful notes for the reviewer. Verbal notices or 
email updates are excellent for initial team communication but do not count as official submissions. 
An official HRIS request must be entered as soon as it is practical to do so. 
2.3 Approval Workflow 
Requests entered into the HRIS route directly to the employee's line manager for evaluation. 
Managers must review these requests promptly, balancing individual requests against team 
workload, upcoming product deadlines, and operational coverage. If a direct manager is out of the 
office, a designated alternate approver will handle incoming requests. Employees receive automated 
alerts when a request is approved or denied. If a request is turned down, the manager must provide 
a clear reason. 
2.4 Leave Balance and Accrual 
Team members can verify their live balances, accrual history, and upcoming time projections anytime 
via the self-service dashboard in the HRIS. Leave credits accrue steadily on a monthly or bi-weekly 
basis depending on your specific payroll cycle. 
Balances, Probation, and Departures 
2.5 Leave Carry-Forward 
Technova actively encourages every employee to use their complete vacation allocation during the 
2026 calendar year. If business needs or personal schedules get in the way, the following rules apply: 
• 
Paid Time Off (PTO): A maximum of 5 unused PTO days can carry forward into the 2027 leave 
year. 
• 
Sick Leave: Unused sick leave can carry forward up to a maximum safety cap of 45 days to 
support employees during unforeseen, long-term medical situations. 
• 
Deadlines: Any carried-forward leave must be used within the first quarter of the new year 
(by March 31, 2027) or it will officially lapse. 
2.6 Leave Encashment

Because we value rest and recovery, Technova does not permit cash payouts for leave days during 
your active employment. Upon formal separation from the company, any accrued and unused PTO 
will be paid out in your final settlement package according to local laws. 
2.7 Leave During Probation Period 
Employees currently serving their introductory probation period will accrue leave credits according 
to standard policy. However, taking elective PTO during the first 90 days is generally discouraged and 
remains subject to strict manager discretion. Sick leave and statutory options remain fully available if 
needed. 
2.8 Leave During Notice Period 
Once an employee enters their resignation notice period, elective leave is generally not permitted. 
Exceptions are made only for verified medical emergencies. Pre-planned leave may be reviewed by 
management and HR on a case-by-case basis. Technova reserves the right to extend the notice 
period by the exact number of leave days taken. 
2.9 Unauthorized Absence 
An unexcused absence lasting three or more consecutive business days without any notification to a 
manager or HR is considered an unauthorized absence. This is handled as job abandonment and can 
result in disciplinary action up to immediate termination. 
2.10 Contact During Leave 
When on leave, you should disconnect from work entirely. Set up an out-of-office auto-reply on your 
email and messaging channels detailing alternative team contacts. Managers will only reach out to 
an employee on leave during a genuine, critical business emergency that no one else can resolve. 
Paid Time Off (PTO) 
3.0 Paid Time Off (PTO) / Annual Leave 
PTO gives our team regular, paid windows to step away from daily tasks to rest, travel, handle 
personal logistics, or recharge. 
3.1 Purpose 
Paid Time Off is vital for maintaining high performance and personal health. We want you to use this 
time for deliberate rest. 
3.2 Eligibility and Entitlement 
All permanent Technova employees are eligible for paid annual leave. Your total yearly entitlement 
scales based on your continuous tenure with the company: 
• 
0 to 2 Years of Service: 18 days of annual PTO. 
• 
2 to 5 Years of Service: 22 days of annual PTO. 
• 
5+ Years of Service: 25 days of annual PTO. 
• 
Part-Time Staff: Entitlements are prorated cleanly based on contracted working hours. 
3.3 Accrual Schedule

PTO builds up progressively each month. For instance, a team member with an 18-day annual 
allowance will see exactly 1.5 days of PTO added to their balance at the completion of each full 
month of service. 
3.4 Planning and Scheduling PTO 
• 
Short Leave: For time off lasting fewer than 5 consecutive business days, log your request at 
least two weeks in advance. 
• 
Long Leave: For absences of 5 or more business days, log your request at least four weeks in 
advance. 
• 
Blackout Windows: During peak product launches or critical client deployment periods, 
Technova may temporarily restrict elective PTO requests to ensure coverage. 
• 
Increments: PTO must be taken in minimum blocks of a half-day (4 hours). 
• 
Negative Balances: Employees cannot run a negative leave balance; your requested time off 
must not exceed your current accrued balance. 
3.5 PTO Case Study: Planning a Vacation 
• 
Scenario: Sarah has crossed 3 years of service at Technova (giving her 22 annual days) and 
wants to take a 10-day summer vacation. 
• 
Action: Six weeks before her trip, Sarah checks her HRIS portal and confirms she has 12 
accrued days available. She enters a formal 10-day request. Her manager reviews the project 
timeline, confirms team coverage is sufficient, and approves it. Sarah configures her out-of-
office notice and logs off cleanly. 
: Sick Leave Guidelines 
4.0 Sick Leave 
Sick leave ensures that employees can prioritize their health or care for immediate family members 
during unexpected illness or medical situations without financial worry. 
4.1 Purpose 
This leave is strictly allocated for recovery from unexpected personal illness, injury, or to attend 
essential medical appointments. 
4.2 Entitlement 
All full-time employees receive 12 days of paid sick leave at the start of each calendar year. Sick leave 
does not accrue monthly; the full 12-day balance is available immediately on January 1, 2026 (or 
prorated appropriately if you join Technova mid-year). 
4.3 Notification Procedure 
If you are too unwell to perform your duties, inform your direct manager via call, text, or email as 
early as possible—ideally before your scheduled start time. A formal sick leave request must be 
entered into the HRIS portal on the day you call out or immediately upon your physical return to 
work. 
4.4 Medical Certification Requirements

• 
Consecutive Days: For any medical call-out lasting three or more consecutive business days, 
you must upload a doctor's note from a registered medical practitioner into the HRIS. 
• 
Certificate Details: The note must explicitly state the dates you were unfit for duty. To 
protect your personal privacy, it should not reveal private diagnostic details. 
• 
Short Absences: Technova reserves the right to request a formal medical note for shorter 
absences if an employee shows a recurring pattern of frequent short-term call-outs. 
4.5 Long-Term Sickness and Returning to Work 
If a severe medical issue requires an extended absence, contact HR to discuss structured options, 
such as corporate disability benefits or an extended unpaid leave of absence. For medical absences 
that exceed 10 consecutive business days, you must provide a formal fitness-to-work certificate 
before resuming active duties to ensure you can return safely. 
4.6 Sick Leave Case Study: Handling an Illness 
• 
Scenario: John wakes up on a Tuesday morning with a severe fever and cannot work. 
• 
Action: At 8:00 AM, John sends a message to his manager detailing his illness. His recovery 
takes four days. On Monday, his first day back, he opens the HRIS, logs a 4-day sick leave 
request, and uploads a digital scan of his doctor's note. 
 Public Holidays and Parental Leaves 
5.0 Public Holidays 
Technova provides paid time off for designated public holidays every year. 
5.1 Official Holiday Schedule 
The company observes 10 paid public holidays each year. The official operational calendar and 
observed dates are published by HR at the start of January. Permanent employees receive full pay for 
these days. 
5.2 Floating Holidays 
When public holidays fall on weekends, Technova will designate an alternate weekday off or provide 
floating holiday credits, allowing teams to maintain a balanced rest schedule. 
6.0 Maternity Leave 
We provide robust support frameworks for expecting mothers to ensure peace of mind during 
childbirth and early infant care. 
6.1 Purpose and Eligibility 
All permanent full-time female employees are eligible for fully paid Maternity Leave. This policy 
ensures adequate recovery time and bonding space without impacting career continuity. 
6.2 Duration and Application 
Maternity leave duration complies fully with or exceeds regional statutory minimums. Employees 
should submit an application in the HRIS at least four weeks before their expected leave date, 
attaching basic medical documentation from their doctor. All standard insurance and employment

benefits continue uninterrupted throughout the leave window. A formal return-to-work plan can be 
coordinated with HR to ensure a smooth ramp-up. 
7.0 Paternity Leave 
Technova recognizes the vital role of partners during the arrival of a new child. 
7.1 Eligibility and Pay 
All permanent employees welcoming a new child via birth or legal adoption are eligible for paid 
Paternity Leave. This leave provides full salary coverage for a designated period, allowing parents to 
focus entirely on family bonding. Requests should be submitted through the HRIS portal ahead of 
time, ensuring clear coordination with your direct team. 
 Bereavement and Civic Duties 
8.0 Bereavement Leave 
We provide compassionate, paid time off to support employees navigating the loss of a loved one. 
8.1 Purpose and Entitlement 
Permanent employees are eligible for paid Bereavement Leave following the passing of an 
immediate or extended family member. This time is provided so employees can attend services, 
handle personal logistics, and grieve with family. 
8.2 Family Definitions and Procedures 
Immediate family includes spouses, children, parents, and siblings. Extended family definitions cover 
grandparents, parents-in-law, and legal guardians. Employees must notify their manager as soon as 
possible and log the request in the HRIS upon their return. Technova prioritizes empathy over 
paperwork, though basic documentation may be requested if needed for administrative records. 
9.0 Jury Duty and Civic Responsibility Leave 
Technova fully supports our team members in fulfilling their civic duties and legal obligations. 
9.1 Purpose and Pay 
We provide fully paid Civic Leave when an employee is officially summoned for jury duty, called as a 
witness, or required by law to participate in public service. Technova will maintain your regular salary 
for the duration of your verified civic service. 
9.2 Documentation 
Employees must upload a copy of the official court summons or civic notice into the HRIS as soon as 
they receive it. If your civic service finishes early on any given day, you are expected to check in with 
your manager or resume remote work if practical. 
Unpaid Leave and Compassionate Care 
10.0 Unpaid Leave of Absence (LOA) 
An Unpaid Leave of Absence allows employees to take extended time away from work for 
exceptional personal reasons when their accrued paid leave balances are exhausted. 
10.1 Eligibility and Review

Permanent employees who have completed their introductory probation period can apply for an 
unpaid LOA. Every application is evaluated individually based on the underlying reason, current team 
workloads, and overall business impacts. 
10.2 Application Process 
Requests must be submitted in writing to your manager and HR at least four weeks in advance, 
detailing the desired duration and reason for the request. Taking an unapproved unpaid absence will 
be managed as an unauthorized departure from your role. 
10.3 Impact on Benefits 
During an extended unpaid LOA, regular salary payments stop. Depending on the length of the 
absence, certain company-sponsored benefits or insurance accruals may be paused or adjusted in 
accordance with local labor laws. Your exact return date and role continuity parameters will be 
confirmed in writing by HR before your leave begins. 
11.0 Compassionate Leave 
Compassionate leave provides dedicated flexibility for employees who need to step away to care for 
a loveSd one navigating a major medical crisis. 
11.1 Purpose and Distinction 
While Bereavement Leave applies specifically to the passing of a family member, Compassionate 
Leave is designed for critical care situations. It applies when an immediate family member suffers a 
sudden, life-threatening illness or severe physical injury, requiring the employee's direct presence 
and care. Log these requests through the HRIS, coordinating closely with HR for any extended care 
planning. 
Special Categories and Responsibilities 
12.0 Special Leave Categories 
Technova provides additional structured leave categories to support unique personal or legal 
obligations. 
12.1 Adoption Leave 
To support teams expanding their families, our Adoption Leave policy offers matching time-off 
parameters to our standard parental leave frameworks, ensuring equitable support for all parents. 
12.2 Voting Leave 
Technova ensures all eligible employees have sufficient time to cast their ballots in local, state, or 
national elections. If your regular working hours overlap significantly with polling hours, coordinate 
with your manager to schedule paid time off to vote. 
12.3 Military Service Leave 
Employees called up for active or reserve military duty will receive a structured leave of absence 
matching all local statutory requirements, protecting their role continuity and seniority. 
13.0 Roles and Responsibilities 
Clear collaboration ensures our leave policies work smoothly across our engineering teams.

13.1 Employee Responsibilities 
• 
Log all leave requests accurately and ahead of time within the HRIS portal. 
• 
Communicate upcoming absences clearly to your team to protect project delivery. 
• 
Set up clear out-of-office notices and hand over critical tasks before logging off. 
13.2 Manager Responsibilities 
• 
Review incoming leave requests fairly and promptly, keeping team metrics in mind. 
• 
Support your team's work-life balance while ensuring operational commitments are met. 
• 
Document clear, objective reasons in the HRIS if a time-off request must be denied. 
13.3 HR Department Responsibilities 
• 
Maintain and update leave frameworks to stay aligned with shifting labor laws. 
• 
Provide clear guidance to managers and teams on complex leave scenarios. 
• 
Securely manage all sensitive medical notes and certification records with strict 
confidentiality. 
FAQs and Administration 
14.0 Policy Administration 
This policy is managed neutrally to ensure consistent, fair application across all business units. 
14.1 Exceptions and Confidentiality 
Any exception to the guidelines in this document requires formal written approval from the Head of 
HR and the Executive Leadership Team. All health records, medical notes, and personal justifications 
shared for leave approvals are treated with high confidentiality and stored securely apart from 
standard corporate directories. 
15.0 Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs) 
Q1: How do I submit a time-off request? A: All leave must be logged through the company's HRIS 
portal. Head to the "Time Off" dashboard, choose your leave category, input your desired dates, and 
submit it to your manager for digital approval. 
Q2: Can my direct manager turn down a PTO request? A: Yes. While Technova encourages taking 
time off, approvals remain subject to active business needs. A manager may decline a request if it 
conflicts directly with critical delivery deadlines or if multiple team members have requested the 
same dates. Your manager must provide a clear reason and work with you to find a better time. 
Q3: What happens if I get sick during a planned PTO vacation? A: If you fall ill for three or more 
consecutive days during your PTO and can provide a valid medical certificate, you can request to 
reclassify those specific days as Sick Leave. Notify your manager immediately and update your entry 
in the HRIS upon your return to credit those PTO days back to your balance. 
Q4: Are public holidays paid days off? A: Yes, all officially designated public holidays are fully paid 
days off for permanent Technova staff. 
16.0 Revision History

Version: 2.0 
• 
Date of Revision: January 1, 2026 
• 
Summary of Changes: Updated comprehensive leave provisions and carry-forward timelines 
for the 2026 calendar year cycle.

1.1 Introduction 
In a modern technology environment, securing corporate digital assets and client data is 
fundamental to business operations. At Technova, we prioritize data privacy, network resilience, and 
robust risk management. 
1.2 Purpose and Scope 
This document outlines the official Information Security and Data Protection Policy for Technova. The 
primary objective is to define a comprehensive framework that protects Technova's information 
assets from all internal, external, deliberate, or accidental threats. This policy applies to all full-time 
and part-time employees, contractors, interns, vendors, and third-party partners who access 
Technova’s corporate networks, computing hardware, cloud infrastructures, or physical premises. 
1.3 Our Core Security Philosophy 
We view information security not as a restrictive barrier, but as an enabling foundation for 
engineering excellence and customer trust. Our security philosophy centers on three core pillars: 
• 
Confidentiality: Ensuring that sensitive systems and private data are accessed only by 
authorized personnel with a legitimate business need. 
• 
Integrity: Protecting information from unauthorized modifications, accidental tampering, or 
malicious corruption to maintain complete data accuracy. 
• 
Availability: Guaranteeing that authorized users have reliable, uninterrupted access to the 
technology infrastructure and engineering applications they need to execute their daily 
work. 
1.4 Compliance and Regulatory Alignment 
Technova aligns its security practices with leading international technology frameworks and data 
privacy standards. This structure ensures that our internal operations comply with relevant local and 
international regulations governing data governance, consumer privacy, and digital infrastructure 
protection. 
2.0 Access Control and Identity Management 
2.1 Access Control Guidelines 
Controlling who can interact with Technova's internal systems reduces our attack surface and 
prevents unauthorized data exposure. 
2.2 The Principle of Least Privilege

Technova enforces the Principle of Least Privilege across all software environments, code 
repositories, and administrative tools. This means that access rights are strictly limited to the bare 
minimum resources required for a team member to complete their specific job duties. Role 
modifications resulting from internal promotions, team transfers, or departmental changes must be 
updated immediately in our corporate directory. 
2.3 Identity Verification and Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) 
All network access to Technova corporate accounts requires strong identity verification. 
• 
MFA Requirement: Multi-Factor Authentication is mandatory for all employees and 
contractors accessing any corporate system, including email, HRIS portals, code 
environments, and cloud consoles. 
• 
Password Standards: Passwords must meet or exceed our modern complexity guidelines, 
requiring a combination of uppercase letters, lowercase letters, numbers, and special 
characters. Passwords must never be reused across separate accounts. 
• 
Shared Accounts: The use of generic or shared group logins is strictly prohibited. Every 
action taken on Technova networks must be traceable to an individual authenticated 
account. 
2.4 Privileged Access Reviews 
Access permissions for high-level administrative accounts, root environments, and core databases 
are subject to continuous monitoring. Human Resources and IT Infrastructure teams conduct formal 
access alignment reviews every quarter to ensure old permissions are stripped away when roles 
change. 
3.0 Device Security and Workstations 
3.1 Endpoint and Workstation Protection 
Every laptop, workstation, and mobile device connected to Technova’s internal networks serves as a 
critical point of protection. 
3.2 Corporate Hardware Allocation 
Employees must perform all work-related duties, software development, and client communications 
exclusively on company-issued computing hardware. Personal devices (laptops, tablets, desktop 
computers) are strictly prohibited from connecting to Technova’s private production environments or 
core development networks. 
3.3 Endpoint Management Protocols 
All company-provided hardware is pre-configured with standardized corporate endpoint security 
software managed directly by our Central IT team. 
• 
Security Software: Endpoint detection, automated firewalls, and corporate anti-malware 
utilities must remain actively running at all times. Employees are strictly prohibited from 
disabling or modifying these applications. 
• 
Software Patching: Operating systems and professional software utilities must be updated 
promptly when corporate alerts are pushed. Critical patches must be installed within 48 
hours of notification.

Encryption: Full-disk encryption is mandatory and automatically enabled on all company-

3.4 Clear Desk and Lock-Screen Discipline 
When leaving your workstation or desk for any duration—even briefly—you must lock your operating 
system screen via keyboard shortcuts or system menus. Physical documents containing confidential 
code, client information, or project strategies must never be left exposed on desks and must be 
stored securely in locked filing cabinets when not in use. 
4.0 Data Classification and Privacy 
4.1 Data Classification Framework 
To protect information efficiently, Technova categorizes data into clear classification levels based on 
its sensitivity and the potential risk of exposure. 
4.2 Tier 1: Public Data 
This category covers information that is intentionally approved for open public consumption. 
Examples include public marketing copy, open career opportunities on our company job board, and 
standardized technical documentation. Exposure of this data presents zero risk to Technova or its 
clients. 
4.3 Tier 2: Internal Operations Data 
This category involves day-to-day business operational data intended exclusively for internal team 
members. Examples include standard operating procedures, non-proprietary engineering templates, 
and internal announcements. Unauthorized external exposure could cause minor operational 
inconvenience but no structural harm. 
4.4 Tier 3: Confidential Corporate Data 
This tier handles sensitive business data that must be kept confidential to protect Technova's 
marketplace position. Examples include corporate financial ledgers, product development roadmaps, 
proprietary source code, and employee personnel files. Unauthorized exposure could lead to severe 
financial or reputational damage. 
4.5 Tier 4: Restricted Client Data 
This represents our highest sensitivity tier, encompassing all client-owned data, production database 
records, consumer personal identifiable information (PII), and authentication keys. This data must 
remain isolated in encrypted storage environments and can only be accessed during active, 
authorized client engineering workflows. 
5.0 Network Security and Data Transmission 
5.1 Network and Communication Safeguards 
Protecting how data travels across internal systems, local offices, and remote spaces prevents 
interception and unauthorized network access. 
5.2 Remote Connection Standards 
Working from remote locations requires secure communication channels to keep corporate traffic 
isolated from public utility hazards.

Corporate VPN: Employees working remotely must utilize the official corporate Virtual

Public Wireless Networks: Connecting to open, public, or unencrypted Wi-Fi networks (such 
as those found in cafes, hotels, or airports) while handling Technova business is strictly 
prohibited unless routed completely through the corporate VPN. 
5.3 Encryption in Transit and at Rest 
All Tier 3 (Confidential Corporate) and Tier 4 (Restricted Client) data must be heavily encrypted 
wherever it moves or is stored. Communication protocols used by our applications must enforce 
modern secure transport layers to safeguard text, API keys, and code updates. 
5.4 Technical Case Study: Insecure Wi-Fi Hazards 
• 
Scenario: An engineer working on a software update at a local coffee shop connects their 
company laptop directly to the shop’s unencrypted public Wi-Fi network without turning on 
their corporate VPN. 
• 
Analysis: This action violates our security protocol. Operating on an open public network 
without a VPN exposes the machine to local interception attacks, potentially allowing 
malicious actors on the same network to monitor clear-text system traffic or harvest active 
session cookies. 
• 
Correct Action: The engineer must activate their secure corporate VPN before connecting to 
any network outside Technova’s private facilities, ensuring all outbound and inbound packets 
are completely encrypted. 
6.0 Software Development and Cloud Security 
6.1 Secure Engineering and Infrastructure 
As a technology company, building security directly into our development lifecycle prevents software 
vulnerabilities and cloud misconfigurations. 
6.2 Secure Coding Standards 
Our engineering teams must adhere to standardized secure coding practices throughout product 
development cycles. This includes validating all input parameters to prevent injection bugs, sanitizing 
output variables, utilizing approved cryptographic libraries, and ensuring authentication methods 
cannot be bypassed. 
6.3 Code Repository Governance 
All proprietary code bases must be hosted within Technova’s authorized secure repositories. 
• 
Secret Management: Hardcoding system passwords, API tokens, database connection 
strings, or SSH keys inside application source code repositories is strictly prohibited. All 
credentials must be managed via dedicated, secure environment secret managers. 
• 
Peer Reviews: All software code updates must undergo a mandatory peer-review process 
and pass automated security vulnerability scans before being merged into active production 
branches.

6.4 Infrastructure and Cloud Isolation 
Technova's production environments are completely isolated from our daily testing and development 
sandboxes. Actual client production data must never be copied, cloned, or downloaded down into 
development or testing environments under any circumstances. 
7.0 Incident Response and Threat Management 
7.1 Threat Identification and Reporting 
Early detection of unusual system behavior, phishing attempts, or physical breaches minimizes 
potential impact and speeds up resolution. 
7.2 Defining a Security Incident 
A security incident is any observable event that compromises our core pillars—such as unauthorized 
access to corporate accounts, active malware infections, laptop theft, suspicious data transfers, or 
potential exposures of client files. 
7.3 Immediate Reporting Procedure 
If you observe a security threat, notice strange behavior on your machine, or accidentally click a 
suspicious link in a phishing email, you must act immediately. 
• 
Report to Security: Send a detailed update directly to our security response team via the 
designated internal dashboard or alert email. 
• 
Include Details: Provide the names of affected systems, exact error messages, screenshots if 
possible, and a brief description of the event. 
• 
Avoid Self-Remediation: Do not attempt to run third-party cleaning tools or manually delete 
system logs yourself, as this can destroy critical evidence needed for forensic investigation. 
7.4 Incident Response Case Study: Phishing Link 
• 
Scenario: An operations specialist receives an email that looks like an urgent request from a 
core vendor asking them to reset their account password. They click the link and enter their 
corporate Technova credentials before realizing the sender domain is fake. 
• 
Analysis: This constitutes an active security compromise that threatens corporate credentials 
and network access. 
• 
Correct Action: The specialist must immediately report the compromise to the security team 
and change their password via our central system right away. The security team will instantly 
terminate all active sessions on that account to block unauthorized entry. 
8.0 Physical and Workplace Security 
8.1 Physical Facility Safeguards 
Digital security depends heavily on physical access controls. Protecting our offices and server rooms 
prevents physical tampering and unauthorized equipment modifications. 
8.2 Badge Discipline and Access Gates 
Access to all Technova office buildings and secure engineering areas is controlled by electronic badge 
access gates.

Individual Badges: Employees must wear their corporate identity badges visibly at all times 
while on company premises. Badges must never be shared or loaned out to anyone. 
• 
No Tailgating: Tailgating—the practice of following another person through a secure door 
without scanning your own badge—is strictly prohibited. Every individual must scan their 
own badge at every entry point. 
8.3 Visitor Management Framework 
All non-Technova personnel, including clients, vendors, delivery staff, and job applicants, must be 
registered as visitors at the front reception desk. Visitors must be issued a temporary visitor badge 
and must remain accompanied by a full-time Technova employee at all times while moving through 
our corporate facilities. 
8.4 Secure Areas and Server Facilities 
Areas holding core local network routers, physical server components, or storage backups are 
designated as high-security zones. Access to these spaces is strictly limited to authorized network 
administrators and requires multi-level authorization logs. 
9.0 Vendor Management and Third-Party Risk 
9.1 Third-Party Risk Governance 
Our security posture is deeply connected to the software applications, SaaS tools, and external 
vendors we utilize to conduct daily operations. 
9.2 Security Due Diligence 
Before Technova integrates any external software tool, cloud platform, or vendor utility into our 
technical operations, the vendor must undergo a formal review by our security evaluation team. 
Vendors must provide verifiable proof of modern security practices, data privacy compliance, and 
robust data encryption standards. 
9.3 Contractual Protections 
All external corporate agreements must include strict data protection clauses. Vendors handling any 
Tier 3 or Tier 4 data are contractually required to report any security or data breach impacting 
Technova systems within 24 hours of discovery. 
10.0 Governance, Administration, and FAQs 
10.1 Individual Employee Obligations 
• 
Complete all mandatory security awareness training modules promptly. 
• 
Identify, flag, and report suspicious emails, system behaviors, or badge violations 
immediately. 
• 
Keep your company-issued laptop physically secure and log out when stepping away. 
10.2 Technical Management Obligations 
• 
Ensure that engineering updates follow our peer review and code validation rules. 
• 
Verify that your team members possess only the access rights required for their active 
project tasks.

Onboarding_and_Joining_Guide 2026 
Effective Date: May 10, 2026 
Version: 1.0 
Approved By: Human Resources Operations and IT Infrastructure Leadership Team. 
1.0 Welcome and Integration Philosophy 
1.1 Welcome to Technova Engineering 
An effective integration process sets the foundation for technical excellence, cultural alignment, and 
long-term career growth. At Technova, we focus on equipping you with the access, context, and 
support systems required to do meaningful work from day one. We want your transition into our 
engineering and operations workspace to be fluid, transparent, and completely free of traditional 
onboarding bottlenecks. 
1.2 Purpose and Scope of This Guide 
This Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) defines the clear, structured steps for welcoming, 
provisioning, and integrating newly hired full-time and part-time staff into Technova. The framework 
ensures a uniform experience across all engineering, administrative, and operations teams. 
Compliance with the milestones detailed in this document is mandatory for all hiring managers, 
internal operations personnel, and engineering leads. 
1.3 Core Pillars of Technova Integration 
Our operational onboarding framework balances technical enablement with human connection, built 
entirely around three core pillars: 
• 
Administrative Clarity: Completing legal identity verification, security documentation, and 
payroll setups smoothly without bureaucratic delays. 
• 
Technical Enablement: Provisioning secure physical equipment and software resource 
accesses quickly so environment configurations can begin immediately. 
• 
Cultural Context: Introducing company values, communication channels, and team 
workflows to build a deep sense of belonging from week one. 
2.0 Pre-Arrival Milestones and Hardware Logistics 
2.1 The Pre-Onboarding Phase 
Our onboarding operations begin the moment a candidate formally accepts an employment offer 
from Technova. Early logistical preparation minimizes processing friction on your official start date. 
2.2 Welcome Communication and Initial Actions 
Human Resources kicks off the workflow by transmitting a personalized confirmation message to the 
incoming team member’s personal email address. This message covers key initial actions: 
• 
Confirmation of the official start date, core team assignment, and direct reporting manager. 
• 
Secure links to upload legal identity documents, signed employment paperwork, and direct 
deposit details into our secure HRIS portal.

• 
Standard office address directions for local team members or shipment tracking parameters 
for fully remote staff. 
2.3 Hardware Provisioning and Deployment Protocols 
The IT Infrastructure and Supply Chain teams coordinate directly to ensure hardware readiness 
ahead of your first day. 
• 
Equipment Allocation: Central IT configures a standard corporate laptop package based on 
your specific department profile (e.g., higher memory configurations for software 
engineering tracks). 
• 
Base Configuration: Every machine undergoes automated imaging, full-disk encryption 
reinforcement, and endpoint security installation before hand-off. 
• 
Delivery Schedule: For remote staff, equipment delivery is scheduled to arrive at your 
confirmed residential address at least 48 hours before your official start date. 
3.0 Day One Framework and Initial System Access 
3.1 Establishing Your Digital Workspace 
Your initial day at Technova focuses on safely activating your corporate identity and validating system 
access paths. 
3.2 Security Authentication and Directory Activation 
At 9:30 AM on your first day, your direct manager or an IT coordinator will guide you through identity 
activation. 
• 
Account Activation: You will receive temporary access tokens to log into your primary 
corporate profile. 
• 
MFA Integration: Setting up Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) via your corporate mobile 
device is mandatory before opening any internal tool. 
• 
Password Initialization: You must immediately replace temporary system credentials with a 
complex, unshared password matching our identity protection rules. 
3.3 Core Communication Tool Provisioning 
Once identity verification passes, automated scripts build out your access to primary internal 
communication utilities, including your corporate email inbox, project hubs, and announcement 
boards. You will also gain full access to the self-service HRIS portal to review leave balances, view 
policy files, and track profile updates. 
4.0 First Week Milestones and Technical Setup 
4.1 Transitioning from Setup to Operations 
The remainder of your first week moves beyond base system access to focus on role-specific context 
and codebase configuration. 
4.2 Manager Alignment and Peer Guides 
Your direct manager will schedule a dedicated initial alignment session during your first 48 hours to 
establish performance expectations and set introductory 30, 60, and 90-day checkpoints. To simplify

your daily adjustment, you will also be paired with an onboarding peer guide from your immediate 
department who will serve as a direct resource for navigating documentation repositories, codebase 
architectures, and internal tools. 
4.3 Code Repository Access and local configurations 
Access to Technova’s repositories is governed by strict identity tracking and the principle of least 
privilege. Managers must submit a digital token request to open permissions for specific systems. 
Once permissions are live, secure cryptographic keys must be generated directly on your corporate 
hardware and registered to your individual account. Engineers must follow our central 
documentation repository rules to install verified code toolchains, local execution runtimes, and 
application dependencies safely. 
4.4 Engineering Setup Case Study: Following Guidelines 
• 
Scenario: A newly joined engineer wants to speed up their local environment configuration. 
They copy a setup script from an unverified public tech blog instead of utilizing the step-by-
step setup guide in the Technova documentation hub. 
• 
Analysis: This action breaks our technical SOP guidelines. Running external, unvetted scripts 
on corporate devices creates a potential entry point for security vulnerabilities or malware. 
• 
Correct Action: The engineer must follow our official, verified internal documentation step-
by-step. If they hit a bug or notice an outdated step in the guide, they should tag their peer 
guide or log an issue inside the internal engineering workspace to get it fixed safely. 
5.0 Training, Feedback loops, and FAQs 
5.1 Completing Mandatory Policy Training 
During your first two weeks of active service, you must complete our baseline security and 
compliance modules through our internal learning platform. This includes a complete review and 
electronic signature of the Technova Employee Handbook and Leave Policy, alongside mandatory 
modules covering information security, data protection rules, and phishing awareness. 
5.2 The New Hire Feedback Loop 
We continuously refine our internal operations based on your direct feedback. At the conclusion of 
your first month, HR will distribute a brief, anonymous survey asking about your onboarding 
experience. We want to know what went perfectly and where we can simplify steps, helping us 
improve the integration path for future team members. 
5.3 Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs) 
Q1: What should I do if my corporate laptop experiences a hardware issue on my first day? A: If 
you run into machine boot issues or screen defects, notify your manager immediately and contact 
our Central IT Helpdesk through our emergency messaging channel or internal support hotline to 
arrange a fast replacement or repair. 
Q2: Am I allowed to update or add sections to the engineering setup guides if I spot a mistake? A: 
Yes! Technova thrives on continuous improvement. If you find an outdated step or discover a clearer 
way to configure a tool while going through your setup, we highly encourage you to update the 
documentation or submit a content update to your team lead.

Q3: Where can I check my current benefits profile or update my direct deposit account details? A: 
All payroll logs, compensation metrics, banking details, and health insurance profiles are managed 
securely within our central self-service HRIS dashboard under your private profile tab.

Procedure for corporate onboarding and joining workflows.
